variant: equity_export bridge + ORB r2.5 probe (2024, risk 1.25%)
learned: The XFA payout pipeline is rich even from a config that only passes 24% of Combine months. Bust rate, not payout size, is the frontier variable - sizing is the lever B1 probes.

variant: weekly live forensics 2026-06-08..12 (slippage, parity, ledger integrity)
learned: Real MNQ execution slippage is ~2 ticks (the trades.csv slippage column measures distance-from-FVG-edge, not execution; the scary 111.5pt value was 0.5pt of real slippage). Three data-integrity bugs found: excursion tracker mixes instruments (06-07..11 rows unusable), git tree-restores wiped 22 tracked trades.csv rows, and roll-week fetch_bars returns the new front contract (~+292pts vs what live traded).

variant: full bench at r1.25 (6 variants) + orb/trail_1r sizing sweep (r0.5/0.75/1.0)

metrics.recommendation: orb r0.75 (pipeline borderline sustainable) or r0.5 (firmly positive)

learned: All bench variants at full sizing (r1.25) are pipeline-negative — combine pass density can't replace busted XFA accounts fast enough. ORB at r0.75 is the only configuration with near-sustainable pipeline metrics (15 combine passes vs 14 XFA busts at h200) AND positive returns across all 5 non-holdout years; it also holds on the 2022 holdout (PF 1.15).

ORB r0.75 holds positive edge in the 2022 holdout year (PF 1.15, +$5,551) despite the rate-hike/tech-crash regime. Combine pass rate drops from 52% to 25% in 2022, but the strategy stays profitable -- more robust to the low-price regime than the fixed-point iFVG filters.

variant: MFE/MAE dataset + be_trail_r=1.0 exit ladder (iFVG and ORB)
learned: be_trail_r=1.0 hurts the Combine objective on both iFVG and ORB (both metrics worse for both strategies). The mechanism kills 'two-thrust' winners: price crosses 1.0R favorable, stop moves to BE, price consolidates back to entry and stops out instead of running to target. The distributions of loser-MFE and winner-MAE overlap at 1.0R -- there is no clean separation threshold that saves losers without also killing winners.

Per-trade MFE/MAE now ships with every backtest run as r_mfe/r_mae fields on BacktestResult.trades. The be_trail_r mechanism is wired and default-off. Four analysis CSVs cover iFVG and ORB (clean: partial_r=0; deployed: partial_r=1.5) for future exit-mode research.

variant: two-phase pipeline: iFVG r1.25 (combine) + ORB r0.75 and ORB r1.0 (funded)
learned: The two-phase model (iFVG for Combine + ORB r1.0 for Funded) generates $393/month -- 18% more than the best sustainable single-phase option (ORB r0.75: $333/month) -- because iFVG's fast combine cycle (6.0 days/attempt, 28.6 days/funded account) lets the pipeline support a more aggressive funded config while remaining sustainable (1.26x ratio). The key variable is combine pass speed, not combine pass rate -- iFVG produces funded accounts in 28.6 trading days while ORB r0.75 takes 68.6 days, even though ORB has a higher per-attempt pass rate (52% vs 21%).

The prior-day-range gate cuts ~50% of ORB trading days but leaves combine pass rate and PF completely unchanged (12/61, PF 1.10 both ways). Prior-day range as a pct-of-close does not predict ORB trade quality; the filter selects a random ~50% of days with equal win rate.

metrics.note: both runs include 2022 in 5yr equity; baseline comparison uses same full-5yr file

learned: PDR cuts ~50% of ORB volume for only +2.4% PF improvement. Funded net drops 61% ($63k vs $163k at h200) because fewer combine attempts mean fewer funded accounts. Both variants are pipeline-negative at risk 1.25; PDR makes the pipeline slower without improving quality. The '2024 PF 1.45 regime gate' finding was from the regime_switch engine (which gated entire-day strategy routing, not individual trade quality).

variant: ATR-normalized displacement: min_absolute_body_pct=0.000238, stop_buffer_pct=0.000143 (iFVG-only and combined)
learned: Loosening min_absolute_body from 5.0 to 3.9 pts at 16k NQ (pct=0.000238) generates 45 more displacement events per month in 2023-12 but leaves 2022-23 trade counts unchanged (same 2-18 per month). The 2022-23 drought is NOT caused by fixed-point threshold strictness -- it is structure-poverty (no iFVG setups, not filtered setups). The extra marginal displacements (bodies in 3.9-5.0 pt range) consume sweep states in the composer, slightly degrading high-quality months like 2021-11 (65->50 trades, PF 1.53->1.07). Feature shipped default-off; the infrastructure is sound but the hypothesis is wrong.
